Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrives at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport to attend the ASEAN Summit in Pasay City, Metro Manila, Philippines. | Photo Credit: Reuters
P rime Minister Narendra Modi is set to participate in the 23rd ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations)-India summit and the 21st East Asia summit on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in Manila. Philippines is hosting the summits in its capacity as the current chair of the 11-nation ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations). In a pre-departure statement, PM Modi said India’s relationship with the ASEAN region is at the “heart of India’s Act East Policy”.
PM Modi is also expected to meet U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the first Quad Summit since 2024 in Manila , on the sidelines of ASEAN summits today (November 17, 2026), sources in New Delhi had confirmed to The Hindu . The meeting would probably take place after Mr. Trump lands in Manila. The confirmation of the Quad Summit in Manila is significant for the Indo-Pacific grouping, and plans to chart out their next course.
Mr. Modi is also scheduled to perform a ground-breaking ceremony for a gurdwara in Manila on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and also interact with members of the Indian community in the Filipino capital, he said on social media.
U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.
This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.
This marks the first in-person, leaders-level Quad gathering since September 2024 in Delaware, as well as the first since Donald Trump returned to the White House.
U.S. President Donald Trump flies into the Philippines on Tuesday ‌at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit.
There could be protests in Manila against Mr. Trump’s visit, after days of demonstrations that have included the burning of effigies of the President and calls for an end to ‌the West Asia war and the scrapping of the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday visited the oldest gurudwara in the Philippines and led the foundation stone-laying ceremony for its redevelopment.
“The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara has stood as a testament to the vibrant India-Philippines cultural and people-to-people ties for over a century,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a social media post.
“ASEAN Leaders and their counterparts from ASEAN’s External Partners convene today in Manila, the Philippines, for the final day of the 49th ASEAN Summit,” ASEAN’s X page said.
“The meetings provide an opportunity to review progress in regional cooperation, exchange views on regional and international developments, and advance partnerships across ASEAN-led mechanisms,” it added.
